<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Sp1nd01" /></noinclude>{{Verse|6|3}} My ſoule is alſo ſore vexed: but thou, O {{sc|Lord}}, how long?

{{Verse|6|4}} Returne, O {{sc|Lord}}, deliuer my ſoule: oh ſaue mee, for thy mercies ſake.

{{Verse|6|5}} {{*}}{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Pſal.30.10. & 88.11 & 115.17. & 118.17. Eſay. 38.18}} For in death {{smaller|there is}} no remembrance of thee: in the graue who ſhall give thee thankes?

{{Verse|6|6}} I am weary with my groning ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, euery night.''}} all the night make I my bed to ſwim: I water my couch with my teares.

{{Verse|6|7}} Mine eie is conſumed becauſe of griefe; it waxeth olde becauſe of all mine enemies.

{{Verse|6|8}} {{*}}{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Mar.7.23. & 25.41. Luc.13.27.}} Depart from me, all yee workers of iniquitie; for the {{sc|Lord}} hath heard the voice of my weeping.

{{Verse|6|9}} The {{sc|Lord}} hath heard my ſupplication; the {{sc|Lord}} will receiue my prayer.

{{Verse|6|10}} Let all mine enemies be aſhamed and ſore vexed: let them returne {{smaller|and}} be aſhamed ſuddainly.

==={{Chapter|7|PSAL. VII.}}===

{{smaller block|[[#7:1|1]] Dauid prayeth againſt the malice of his enemies, profeſsing his innocency. [[#7:10|10]] By faith he ſeeth his defence and the deſtruction of his enemies.}}

¶ Shiggaion of Dauid; which he ſang vnto the {{sc|Lord}} concerning the ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, buſines.''}} words of Cuſh the Beniamite.

{{Verse|7|1|notext=}} {{dropinitial|O|image=King James Bible (1611) page A5r (O).png|imgsize=100px}} {{sc|Lord}}, my God, in thee doe I put my truſt: ſaue me from all them that perſsecute me, and deliuer me.

{{Verse|7|2}} Leaſt hee teare my ſoule like a lyon, renting {{smaller|it}} in pieces, while {{smaller|there is}} †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Heb not a deliuerer.''}} none to deliuer.

{{Verse|7|3}} O {{sc|Lord}} my God, if I haue done this; if there be iniquitie in my hands:

{{Verse|7|4}} If I haue rewarded euill vnto him that was at peace with me: (yea I haue deliuered him that without cauſe is mine enemie.)

{{Verse|7|5}} Let the enemie perſecute my ſoule, and take {{smaller|it}}, yea let him tread downe my life vpon the earth, and lay mine honour in the duſt. Selah.

{{Verse|7|6}}  Ariſe, O {{sc|Lord}}, in thine anger, lift vp thy ſelfe, becauſe of the rage of mine enemies: and awake for me to the iudgement {{smaller|that}} thou haſt commanded.

{{Verse|7|7}} So ſhall the congregation of the people compaſſe thee about: for their ſakes therefore returne thou on high.

{{Verse|7|8}} The Lord ſhal iudge the people, iudge me, O {{sc|Lord}}, *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Pſal 18.19.}} according to my righteouſneſſe, and according to mine integritie {{smaller|that}} is in me.

{{Verse|7|9}} Oh let the wickednes of the wicked come to an end, but eſtabliſh the iust: *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* 1.Sam.16.7.1.Chr.28.9.pſal.139.1 Ierem.11.20.and 17.10.and 20.12.}} for the righteous God trieth the hearts and reines.

{{Verse|7|10}} †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Heb. my buckler is vpon God.''}} My defence {{smaller|is}} of God, which ſaueth the vpright in heart.

{{Verse|7|11}} ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, God ''is'' a rightoeous Iudge.''}} God iudgeth the righteous, and God is angrie {{smaller|with the wicked}} euery-day.

{{Verse|7|12}} If he turne not, he will whet his ſword: he hath bent his bowe, and made it ready.

{{Verse|7|13}} He hath alſo prepared for him the inſtruments of death: he ordaineth his arrowes againſt the perſecutors.

{{Verse|7|14}} {{*}}{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Iob 15.35.Eſa.59.4 Iam.1.15.}} Behold, he trauelleth with iniquitie, and hath couceiued miſchiefe, and brought forth falſhood.

{{Verse|7|15}} †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Heb. hee hath digged a pit.''}} He made a pit and digged it, *
{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Pſal.9.15. and 10.2. prou.5.22.}} and is fallen into the ditch {{smaller|which}} he made.

{{Verse|7|16}} His miſchiefe ſhall returne vpon his owne head, and his violent dealing ſhall come downe vpon his owne pate.

{{Verse|7|17}} I will praiſe the {{sc|Lord}} according to his righteouſneſſe: and will ſing {{smaller|praiſe}} to the name of the {{sc|Lord}} moſt high.

==={{Chapter|8|PSAL. VIII.}}===

{{smaller block|Gods glory is magnified by his works, and by his loue to man.}}

¶ To the chiefe Muſicion vpon Gittith, a Pſalme of Dauid

{{Verse|8|1|notext=}} {{dropinitial|O|image=King James Bible (1611) page A2r (O).png|imgsize=100px}} {{sc|Lord}} our Lord, how excellent {{smaller|is}} thy name in all the earth! who haſt ſet thy glory aboue the heauens.

{{Verse|8|2}} *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Mat.21.16.}}Out of the mouth of babes and ſucklings haſt thou †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Heb. founded.''}} ordained ſtrength, becauſe of thine enemies, that thou mighteſt ſtill the enemie and auenger.

{{Verse|8|3}} When I conſider thy heauens, the worke of thy fingers, the moone and the ſtarres which thou haſt ordained;

{{Verse|8|4}} *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=*Iob 7.17. pſal.144.3. ''Heb.''2.6.}}What {{smaller|is}} man, that thou art mindfull of him? and the ſonne of man, that thou viſiteſt him?

{{Verse|8|5}} For thou haſt made him a little lower then the Angels; and haſt crowned him with glory and honour.

{{Verse|8|6}} Thou madeſt him to haue dominion ouer the workes of thy hands; *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* 1.Cor.15.27.}}thou haſt put all {{smaller|things}} vnder his feete.

{{Verse|8|7}} †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Heb.flocks and oxen, all of them.''}} All ſheepe and oxen, yea and the beasſts of the field.
